what: Riot Platforms runs large-scale computing facilities. It mines bitcoin at sites in Texas and Kentucky and is converting part of its capacity to host artificial-intelligence computing, where customers pay to lease power and space rather than the company earning bitcoin.
customers: On the mining side there is no customer: Riot earns bitcoin by running machines. On the data centre side, AI and high-performance computing companies leasing power and space under long-term agreements.
money: Bitcoin mined by its own machines, worth whatever bitcoin is worth on the day.
Electrical equipment manufacturing, and hosting and leasing capacity to third parties.
moat: Riot holds very large blocks of contracted electrical power with approved grid connections, which take years to obtain and are now the scarce input in AI computing. Its Texas sites also participate in grid demand-response programmes, earning payments for reducing consumption when the grid is stressed.
risks: The trailing twelve months show a net loss of about $1.4B and free cash flow of roughly negative $901.1M. Spending vastly exceeds income.
Cash of $233.5M against $866.8M of debt is thin for this rate of capital spending, so more financing is near certain and usually means issuing shares.
The shares trade at about 9.8 times sales while the company is deeply loss-making.
Bitcoin's price and the network difficulty adjustment determine mining revenue, and neither can be influenced.
Twenty-two analysts average a $32.52 target against a $17.73 price. On a business burning this much cash, such a gap reflects speculation about contracts not yet signed.
opportunities: Revenue grew strongly, from $376.7M in 2024 to $647.4M in 2025, with trailing revenue of about $675.7M.
Converting mining capacity to AI computing raises revenue per megawatt substantially and makes it contracted rather than dependent on bitcoin.
Power capacity with grid interconnection is the binding constraint on AI data centre growth, and Riot owns a lot of it.
The company holds a large quantity of mined bitcoin on its balance sheet, which rises in value with the asset.
watch: Signed AI hosting contracts and megawatts delivered. Mining results follow bitcoin and tell you nothing about management; converting power into long-term leases is the only thing that justifies the current valuation.
